hello.note: A polite hello at any time of day. Ciao (chow) is casual, for friends and people you know

good-morning.note: Used until the afternoon, then buonasera (bwoh-nah-SEH-rah). Greet shop staff with it as you walk in

goodbye.note: Buona giornata (BWOH-nah jor-NAH-tah) means have a good day

thank-you.note: Grazie mille (MEEL-leh) means thanks a lot. The reply is prego (PREH-goh)

yes.note: The accent mark tells it apart from si, meaning oneself

excuse-me.note: Also gets a waiter's attention. Permesso (pehr-MEHS-soh) is for getting past someone

my-name.note: Literally "I call myself". The audio uses Peter as the example name

speak-slowly.note: Parli is the polite (Lei) form of speak

repeat.note: Può means can you, in the polite form

speak-english.note: Parla is the polite form of you speak

four.note: Say a double consonant for a beat longer, as in the tt here

how-much.note: For more than one item say Quanto costano? (KOS-tah-noh)

would-like.note: The polite way to order. The audio uses un caffè as the example

i-want.note: Blunt in Italian; vorrei is politer. The audio uses questo (this) as the example

do-you-have.note: Said to the shop as a whole. To one person use Ha...? (ah). The audio uses dell'acqua (water) as the example

ill-take-it.note: For a feminine item say la prendo

too-expensive.note: Troppo cara for something feminine, such as una borsa

discount.note: Haggling works at markets, not in shops

bill.note: In Italy the bill only comes when you ask for it

checkout-time.text: A che ora è il check-out?
checkout-time.say: ah keh OH-rah eh eel CHEK-owt

wifi.text: Qual è la password del wifi?

toilet.note: "Dov'è …?" means "where is …?" for anything. Signs may say toilette or servizi

bus.note: A long-distance coach is un pullman (POOL-mahn)

train-station.note: La stazione alone is what people usually say

which-train.note: Swap in any city; the audio uses Hanoi as the example

buy-ticket.note: Paper train tickets must be stamped in the small machine on the platform before you board

two-tickets.note: The audio uses Hanoi as the example city
two-tickets.spoken: Posso comprare due biglietti per Hanoi?

trip-length.note: The audio uses Hanoi as the example city
trip-length.spoken: Quanto dura il viaggio per Hanoi?

allergic.note: Women say allergica (ahl-LEHR-jee-kah). Add the food: ai frutti di mare (seafood), alle noci (nuts), alle uova (eggs). The audio uses frutti di mare as the example
allergic.spoken: Sono allergico ai frutti di mare

love-dish.note: Mi piace tantissimo (mee PYAH-cheh) means I like it so much

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.text: Un tavolo per due, per favore
table-for-two.say: oon TAH-voh-loh pehr DOO-eh pehr fah-VOH-reh
table-for-two.note: For more people use tre (3) or quattro (4) instead of due

beer.text: Una bottiglia di birra, per favore
beer.say: OO-nah boht-TEE-lyah dee BEER-rah pehr fah-VOH-reh
beer.note: Una birra alla spina (SPEE-nah) is a draught beer

coffee.note: It is a small espresso. Cappuccino (kap-poo-CHEE-noh) is for the morning; Italians rarely order it after a meal

water.note: Naturale (nah-too-RAH-leh) is still, and frizzante (free-DZAHN-teh) is sparkling

cheers.note: Cin cin (cheen cheen) is also common

help.note: Shout it. The police are la polizia (lah poh-lee-TSEE-ah)
